1.2 Admission and Cessation of Membership

(a) Applications for membership shall be made in writing to the Membership Secretary, on such forms as may be prescribed from time to time.

(b) The Management Committee shall have the power to accept or reject any application for membership, provided that no application shall be rejected without giving the applicant an opportunity to make representations.

(c) Membership shall cease upon the death of the member, upon resignation in writing to the Membership Secretary, or upon termination by the Management Committee for conduct detrimental to the Association.

(d) A member whose conduct is considered detrimental may be suspended or expelled by a resolution of the Management Committee, provided that the member shall have the right to be heard before any such decision is made.

(e) Any member may resign by giving one month's notice in writing to the Membership Secretary, subject to the payment of any outstanding subscriptions.

1.3 Subscriptions

(a) The annual subscription for each category of membership shall be determined at the Annual General Meeting and shall be payable on or before 1 April each year.

(b) The Management Committee may, at its discretion, waive or reduce subscriptions in cases of hardship.

(c) Members whose subscriptions are more than three months in arrears shall be deemed to have lapsed their membership, provided that the Membership Secretary shall have given written notice of the arrears.

---

2. OFFICERS AND MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE

2.1 Officers

The Officers of the Association shall be:

(a) Chairperson
(b) Vice-Chairperson
(c) Treasurer
(d) Secretary
(e) Membership Secretary

2.2 Election of Officers

(a) All Officers shall be elected annually at the Annual General Meeting from among the Full Members and Honorary Life Members.

(b) Nominations for Officers shall be submitted in writing to the Secretary at least 14 days before the Annual General Meeting, with the consent of the nominee.

(c) If no nomination is received for any office, nominations may be taken from the floor at the Annual General Meeting.

(d) No person shall hold the office of Treasurer for more than six consecutive years, unless no other person is willing to stand.

2.3 Management Committee

(a) The affairs of the Association shall be managed by a Management Committee comprising the Officers and up to six other members elected at the Annual General Meeting.

(b) The Management Committee shall meet at least once every two months, and may meet more frequently as required.

(c) The quorum for a meeting of the Management Committee shall be five members, of whom at least two shall be Officers.

(d) The Management Committee may co-opt additional members with voting rights, provided that no more than two co-opted members serve at any one time. Co-opted members shall serve until the next Annual General Meeting.

(e) The Management Committee shall have the power to appoint sub-committees for specific purposes and to delegate such powers as it sees fit. All sub-committees shall report to the Management Committee.
(c) The minutes of each General Meeting shall be approved at the next General Meeting and signed by the Chairperson of that meeting as a correct record.

4. FINANCIAL PROVISIONS

4.1 Financial Year

The financial year of the Association shall run from 1 April to 31 March in each year.

4.2 Banking

(a) The funds of the Association shall be held in a bank account or accounts in the name of the Association.

(b) Cheques and other instruments of payment shall be signed by any two of the following Officers: the Treasurer, the Chairperson, the Secretary, and the Vice-Chairperson. No single signatory shall be a member of the same immediate family as another signatory.

(c) The Management Committee shall have power to open, operate and close bank accounts and to authorise electronic banking facilities, provided that all payments are authorised in accordance with the procedures set out in this clause.

4.3 Accounts and Audit

(a) The Treasurer shall keep proper books of account showing all financial transactions of the Association, and shall present a statement of income and expenditure and a balance sheet to the Annual General Meeting in each year.

(b) The accounts shall be examined annually by an independent examiner appointed at the Annual General Meeting, who shall not be a member of the Management Committee. The examiner shall report to the members on the accounts.

(c) The Management Committee may, at its discretion, engage a professional accountant to prepare or audit the accounts.

4.4 Financial Controls

(a) The Treasurer shall prepare a budget for the forthcoming financial year for approval by the Management Committee no later than the first meeting of that year.

(b) The Management Committee shall approve all expenditure exceeding five hundred pounds, other than routine expenditure provided for in the approved budget.

(c) No Officer or member of the Management Committee shall be entitled to receive any payment from the funds of the Association other than reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses properly incurred in the conduct of Association business, provided that such reimbursement is approved by the Management Committee.

(d) The Association may, with the approval of the Management Committee, make grants or donations to other organisations or individuals whose purposes are consistent with the objectives of the Association.

(e) The Management Committee shall arrange for the accounts to be reviewed at least quarterly and shall report on the financial position of the Association to each General Meeting.

4.5 Insurance and Indemnity

(a) The Association shall maintain public liability insurance and such other insurance as the Management Committee considers appropriate.

(b) The Association may indemnify any Officer or member of the Management Committee against any liability incurred in the proper performance of their duties, to the extent permitted by law.

5. AMENDMENTS TO THE CONSTITUTION

(a) This constitution may be amended by a resolution passed by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting at a General Meeting, provided that notice of the proposed amendment has been given in writing to the Secretary at least twenty-one days before the meeting.

(b) The notice of the proposed amendment shall be circulated to all members with the notice of the meeting.

(c) No amendment shall be made which would cause the Association to cease to be a community amateur sports club within the meaning of the relevant tax legislation, or which would alter the objects of the Association to a material extent without the prior written consent of the members.

(d) The current version of this constitution was adopted at an Extraordinary General Meeting held on 14 April 2021, and shall remain in force until amended in accordance with this clause. The previous version, adopted on 3 July 2009, is superseded and shall have no further effect.

6. DISSOLUTION
6. DISSOLUTION

(a) The Association may be dissolved by a resolution passed by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting at a General Meeting, provided that notice of the resolution has been given in writing to the Secretary at least twenty-one days before the meeting.

(b) Upon dissolution, the Management Committee shall, after satisfying all debts and liabilities of the Association, dispose of any remaining assets in the following manner:

(i) if the Association is, at the time of dissolution, a community amateur sports club registered with Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs, any surplus assets shall be applied for charitable purposes, or for the purposes of sport, or for the purposes of community recreation, as the members may decide at the meeting at which the resolution for dissolution is passed, or failing such decision, as the Management Committee shall decide in accordance with the advice of the club's auditors or independent examiner;

(ii) in any other case, the surplus assets shall be transferred to another organisation whose purposes are consistent with the objects of the Association, or to a registered charity, as the members shall decide.

(c) A copy of the resolution for dissolution shall be sent to Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs within twenty-eight days of its passing, if the Association is a registered community amateur sports club.

(d) The Management Committee shall be responsible for the winding up of the affairs of the Association and for the preparation of a final statement of accounts, which shall be presented to the final General Meeting of the Association.

7. INTERPRETATION

(a) In this constitution, unless the context otherwise requires:

"the Association" means Wrekin Vale Community Sports Association;

"the Committee" and "the Management Committee" mean the committee appointed in accordance with clause 4.1;

"General Meeting" means an Annual General Meeting or an Extraordinary General Meeting called in accordance with clause 3.5;

"member" means a person whose application for membership has been accepted in accordance with clause 2.1, and whose membership has not lapsed or been terminated;

"Officer" means the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, Secretary, Treasurer, or such other office as the Management Committee may from time to time create;

"the Secretary" includes any person appointed to act in the absence of the Secretary;

"the objects" means the objects set out in clause 1.1;

"written" includes electronic communication, provided that the sender can reasonably be expected to receive a record of the communication.

(b) Words importing the singular shall include the plural and vice versa, and words importing any gender shall include all genders.

(c) Clause headings are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this constitution.

(d) Any reference to a statutory provision includes any subsequent re-enactment or modification of that provision.

(e) If any provision of this constitution is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.

8. ADOPTION AND SUPERSESSION

(a) This constitution, being the current version, was adopted at an Extraordinary General Meeting held on 14 April 2021. It shall come into force immediately upon adoption.

(b) This constitution supersedes and replaces the previous version of the constitution of the Association adopted on 3 July 2009. The previous version shall have no further effect from the date of adoption of this constitution.

(c) For the avoidance of doubt, all actions taken and appointments made under the previous version of the constitution prior to 14 April 2021 shall be deemed to have been validly taken and made, and shall continue in force as if taken and made under this constitution, except to the extent that they are inconsistent with this constitution.

(d) The minutes of the Extraordinary General Meeting held on 14 April 2021 shall record the adoption of this constitution and the names of the members present.

This policy applies to:

- All WVCSA-affiliated teams and activity groups (including football, cricket, netball, and the

PRINCIPLES

1. The welfare of the child or vulnerable adult is paramount.
2. All participants, regardless of age, ability, gender, race, religion, sexual orientation, or
   background, have a right to enjoy sport in a safe and positive environment.
3. All suspicions and allegations of abuse will be taken seriously and responded to swiftly,
   fairly, and in accordance with local safeguarding children board procedures.
4. All staff and volunteers are responsible for their own conduct and for reporting concerns.
5. Confidentiality will be respected, but never at the expense of protecting a child or
   vulnerable adult from harm.

KEY ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Safeguarding Officer: Holds overall responsibility for the implementation of this policy, for
maintaining the safeguarding records, for ensuring that appropriate DBS checks are completed, and
for acting as the first point of contact for any safeguarding concern. The current Safeguarding
Officer is Margaret Hesketh.

Deputy Safeguarding Officer: Supports the Safeguarding Officer and acts in their absence. The
current Deputy is Alan Preece.

Club Welfare Officer (Junior Sections): Responsible for promoting good practice and welfare
awareness among junior coaches and parents. Current post holder: Mrs. D. Iqbal.

All Coaches, Helpers, and Volunteers: Responsible for familiarising themselves with this policy,
for undertaking required training, and for reporting any concern to the Safeguarding Officer or
Deputy without delay.

Management Committee: Responsible for ensuring that adequate resources are available to implement
this policy and for reviewing safeguarding reports at least annually.

PROCEDURE FOR REPORTING A CONCERN

Any person who has a concern about the welfare of a child or vulnerable adult must report it on
the same day, wherever possible, to the Safeguarding Officer. If the concern relates to the
Safeguarding Officer personally, the report must be made to the Deputy Safeguarding Officer or to
the Chair of the Management Committee.

The reporting person should not investigate the concern themselves, should not discuss it with the
person alleged to have caused harm, and should not inform the parents/carers without advice from
the Safeguarding Officer or from the local authority children’s services.

The Safeguarding Officer will record the concern on a Confidential Incident Report Form (Form
WVCSA-SF1), will make an initial assessment, and will refer to Shropshire Children’s Services or
the Police where the threshold for referral is met. All referrals will be confirmed in writing
within 24 hours.

RECRUITMENT AND DBS CHECKS

All volunteers and paid staff who have regular or unsupervised access to children or vulnerable
adults are required to hold an enhanced DBS certificate with barred list check, or to be registered
with the DBS update service. New appointments must not begin work with children until a clear
check has been received. The Safeguarding Officer maintains a DBS Register (Appendix A of this
policy).

TRAINING REQUIREMENTS

All coaches and volunteers with direct contact with children must complete:

- Safeguarding Awareness Training (face-to-face or online, minimum 3 hours) within 3 months of
  starting.
- Refresher training every 3 years.
- Safeguarding for Committee Members (online module) for all committee members.

documents.content:
This policy applies to:

- All WVCSA-affiliated teams and activity groups (including football, cricket, netball, and the
  junior athletics section).
- All hired-out facilities and third-party bookings where WVCSA has safeguarding responsibility
  under the hire agreement.
- All trips, tournaments, and residential events organised by the Association.
- Any digital or online activity conducted in the name of the Association, including social media
  groups and video calls.

PRINCIPLES

1. The welfare of the child or vulnerable adult is paramount.
2. All participants, regardless of age, ability, gender, race, religion, sexual orientation, or
   background, have a right to enjoy sport in a safe and positive environment.
3. All suspicions and allegations of abuse will be taken seriously and responded to swiftly,
   fairly, and in accordance with local safeguarding children board procedures.
4. All staff and volunteers are responsible for their own conduct and for reporting concerns.
5. Confidentiality will be respected, but never at the expense of protecting a child or
   vulnerable adult from harm.

KEY ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Safeguarding Officer: Holds overall responsibility for the implementation of this policy, for
maintaining the safeguarding records, for ensuring that appropriate DBS checks are completed, and
for acting as the first point of contact for any safeguarding concern. The current Safeguarding
Officer is Margaret Hesketh.

Deputy Safeguarding Officer: Supports the Safeguarding Officer and acts in their absence. The
current Deputy is Alan Preece.

Club Welfare Officer (Junior Sections): Responsible for promoting good practice and welfare
awareness among junior coaches and parents. Current post holder: Mrs. D. Iqbal.

All Coaches, Helpers, and Volunteers: Responsible for familiarising themselves with this policy,
for undertaking required training, and for reporting any concern to the Safeguarding Officer or
Deputy without delay.

Management Committee: Responsible for ensuring that adequate resources are available to implement
this policy and for reviewing safeguarding reports at least annually.

The safeguarding records note that Wrekin Vale Community Sports Association Safeguarding Policy last_review_date was 2023-11-20. Record status: current.

PROCEDURE FOR REPORTING A CONCERN

Any person who has a concern about the welfare of a child or vulnerable adult must report it on
the same day, wherever possible, to the Safeguarding Officer. If the concern relates to the
Safeguarding Officer personally, the report must be made to the Deputy Safeguarding Officer or to
the Chair of the Management Committee.

The reporting person should not investigate the concern themselves, should not discuss it with the
person alleged to have caused harm, and should not inform the parents/carers without advice from
the Safeguarding Officer or from the local authority children’s services.

The Safeguarding Officer will record the concern on a Confidential Incident Report Form (Form
WVCSA-SF1), will make an initial assessment, and will refer to Shropshire Children’s Services or
the Police where the threshold for referral is met. All referrals will be confirmed in writing
within 24 hours.

RECRUITMENT AND DBS CHECKS

All volunteers and paid staff who have regular or unsupervised access to children or vulnerable
adults are required to hold an enhanced DBS certificate with barred list check, or to be registered
with the DBS update service. New appointments must not begin work with children until a clear
check has been received. The Safeguarding Officer maintains a DBS Register (Appendix A of this
policy).

TRAINING REQUIREMENTS

All coaches and volunteers with direct contact with children must complete:

- Safeguarding Awareness Training (face-to-face or online, minimum 3 hours) within 3 months of
  starting.
- Refresher training every 3 years.
- Safeguarding for Committee Members (online module) for all committee members.

Records of training are held in Section 3 of these Safeguarding Records.

**Safeguarding Records – Extract 4 of 4**

**Incident Report – IR-2024-03**

**Report No:** 2024-03
**Date Received:** 22/03/2024
**Received By:** Margaret Osei (Safeguarding Officer)
**Name of Individual Involved:** T. Hussain (Parent of U11 player)
**Role:** Parent / Spectator
**Date of Incident:** 21/03/2024, approx. 18:45
**Location:** Clubhouse car park, during U11 training session

**Nature of Concern:**
Following a training session, a parent reported that T. Hussain had approached another parent in the car park and made a verbal threat regarding a disagreement over match selection. The incident was witnessed by two other parents and one coach (P. Singh, U11 Coach). No physical contact was reported. The parent who was threatened stated they did not feel safe returning to the club for the remainder of the season.

**Action Taken:**
1. T. Hussain was contacted by the Safeguarding Officer on 23/03/2024 and the club’s code of conduct for spectators was read to them over the phone. They acknowledged the content.
2. A written warning was issued on 24/03/2024, confirming that any further breach would result in a temporary suspension from attending matches and training.
3. The parent who raised the concern was offered a point of contact for further support and was informed of the outcome.
4. The club Welfare Officer, S. Patel, was copied into all correspondence.
5. Incident was discussed at the committee meeting on 02/04/2024. It was agreed that the club would place a notice in the next newsletter reminding all spectators of the code of conduct.

**Status:** Closed – written warning issued and acknowledged. No further incidents reported as of 30/04/2024.

---

**Incident Report – IR-2024-04**

**Report No:** 2024-04
**Date Received:** 11/04/2024
**Received By:** Margaret Osei (Safeguarding Officer)
**Name of Individual Involved:** L. Bennett (First Aid Lead – Football)
**Role:** Volunteer (First Aid Lead)
**Date of Incident:** 10/04/2024, approx. 19:20

**Nature of Concern:**
A parent of a U9 player contacted the club to report that during a match, a child who had sustained a head injury was not assessed by the first aid lead for approximately 15 minutes. The parent stated that L. Bennett was seen attending to another child at the time and that the injured child was left sitting on the touchline. The parent also noted that the incident was not recorded in the match day first aid log.

**Action Taken:**
1. L. Bennett was spoken to on 12/04/2024. They confirmed that they were attending to a separate injury and were not aware that the head injury had not been flagged by the coach.
2. The club’s concussion and head injury protocol was reviewed. It was identified that the protocol did not specify a maximum response time for a first aid lead to attend to a reported injury. This gap was noted for the next policy review.
3. L. Bennett has been asked to ensure that any incident where they are delayed in attending is logged in the match day log with a note of the reason.
4. The parent was contacted and the club apologised for the delay. The parent accepted the apology and did not wish to escalate further.

**Status:** Closed – procedural gap identified and logged for policy review. L. Bennett remains in post and has confirmed understanding of the expectation.

---

**Policy Review Note – PR-2024-02**

**Policy Under Review:** Safeguarding Children and Young People Policy (Version 3.1)
**Date of Review:** 02/04/2024
**Review Lead:** Margaret Osei (Safeguarding Officer)
**Attendees:** S. Patel (Welfare Officer), J. Whitmore (Treasurer), R. Fletcher (Grounds Staff), P. Singh (Coach – U11)

**Summary of Discussion:**
The committee reviewed the policy in light of the incident involving a spectator (IR-2024-03). It was agreed that the policy currently does not contain a specific section on spectator conduct at training sessions, only at matches. The following amendment was proposed and approved:

**Amendment:** Add a new sub-section under “Behaviour and Conduct” titled “Spectators at Training Sessions”, which will state that the same code of conduct applies to spectators attending training as to those attending matches, and that the club reserves the right to issue written warnings and temporary bans for breaches.
